clue.text: Holiday little bit warmer?

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, as in 'not a whit'
the sun is what warms us

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a holiday might be a touch warmer.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitsun is the British name for Pentecost, traditionally marked by a public holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitsun is a Christian festival seven weeks after Easter, long a British bank holiday weekend.

clue.text: Coiled snake for a start causes injury

parts.note: wound, as in wound up, means coiled

indicators.note: the start of the word snake, its first letter, is taken

explanation.surface: A coiled snake strikes first and hurts someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To wound is to inflict harm on the body, so 'wounds' and 'causes injury' are verb synonyms.

clue.text: Funding raised in hotel restaurant?

indicators.note: the turned-up word sits in the hotel's letters

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: aid is funding or financial help

explanation.surface: Money is raised in a hotel's restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: in Britain 'an Indian' is a curry house.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage 'an Indian' is a restaurant serving South Asian food, a colloquial shortening.

clue.text: Extraordinary as Grail held — by him?

definitions.text: Extraordinary as Grail held — by him?

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: had is the past tense of have, meaning held

explanation.surface: A remarkable claim that the Holy Grail was held by a particular man.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad is the Arthurian knight who, in legend, achieved the quest for the Holy Grail.

clue.text: 2 Down leader once lifted helium-filled vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the letters are read upwards
the vessel is filled with the element, holding it inside

parts.note: an urn is a vessel
He is the chemical symbol for helium

explanation.surface: A former leader floats skyward on a helium balloon.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 Down is INDIAN, so the definition is an Indian leader of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of independent India, serving until 1964.

clue.text: Take little dog round on ship for exercise

indicators.note: with 'round', to take one thing round another is to wrap it about the other pieces
the dog's letters go round the others, enclosing them

parts.note: a pup is a young dog
on, meaning about or concerning, is RE
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: An instruction to walk a puppy around the deck of a ship to keep fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A press-up is a floor workout pushing the body up with the arms, a standard exercise.

clue.text: Secretary off again to arid tableland

parts.note: PA, personal assistant, is a secretary

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A secretary heads off again to a dry plateau.
explanation.definitionFit: Patagonia is the region of southern Argentina and Chile, much of it a dry steppe plateau.

clue.text: Constant smoker's Greek character touring north

indicators.note: the Greek letter tours round the other one, enclosing it

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A chain-smoking Greek eccentric travels northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constant smoker' sounds like a person; it is the ever-smoking Sicilian volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is an active Sicilian volcano that almost always emits a plume of smoke.

clue.text: Still holding an old penny piece

indicators.note: the word for still holds the other letters within it

parts.note: serene means still or calm
an gives A
D was the abbreviation for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: Someone is still clutching an old penny coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' looks like a coin to go with the penny; here it is a musical piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a piece of music, traditionally sung at evening beneath a lover's window.

clue.text: Liking to write slogan

parts.note: to pen is to write
a chant is a slogan shouted repeatedly

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys composing slogans.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong taste or fondness for something.

clue.text: Dispenser of milk shake Juliet refused

indicators.note: the letter for Juliet is turned away, so it is dropped from the word

parts.note: to judder is to shake violently
J is Juliet in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A milk dispenser shakes, and a woman named Juliet declines a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow's udder is the gland from which milk is drawn, so it dispenses milk.

clue.text: Hard nut in bizarre accident

indicators.note: something bizarre is twisted out of its normal shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tough nut lodged in some strange mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit-and-run is a road accident whose driver flees without stopping.

clue.text: Drink and drive conveying a tense playwright

indicators.note: to convey is to carry, so the drink-and-drive pieces carry the others inside them

parts.note: a dram is a small drink of spirits
an urge is an inner drive
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A warning about drink-driving that somehow involves a nervous dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramaturge is a writer or adviser for the theatre, a dramatist by another name.

clue.text: Island of no great length?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in Scotland an ... is a small island
second meaning: a short unit of length

explanation.walkthrough: Inch for an island is a Scottish usage, seen in names like Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small Scottish isle and a tiny imperial measure of about two and a half centimetres.

clue.text: A heartless romance and trouble for lover

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a romance is a work of fiction
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted love affair brings trouble to a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lover' suggests romance, but it means an enthusiast, a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: An aficionado is an ardent devotee or fan of a pursuit, a lover of it.

clue.text: Duck fine among bats endangered in paradise

indicators.note: the two short pieces are set among the rearranged letters
bats means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A duck and some endangered bats share an idyllic setting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garden of Eden is the Biblical first home of Adam and Eve, the archetype of paradise.

clue.text: Daughter Ann holding up drunk gets a wine

indicators.note: the name holds the turned word inside it
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: oiled is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A daughter named Ann props up a drunk and is given wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandelion wine is a homemade country wine fermented from the flower's petals.

clue.text: Maestro out to cage minute monkey

indicators.note: the reshuffled letters cage the extra letter, enclosing it
out means wrong or misplaced, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A conductor sets out to trap a tiny monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' reads as tiny, describing the monkey; it is the time unit's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmoset is a small South American primate, a kind of monkey.

clue.text: Panda one of four young in pit

indicators.note: the young one goes in the pit's letters

parts.note: a scar is a mark such as a pockmark or pit
a quad is a quadruplet, one of four babies born together

explanation.surface: A panda cub, one of a litter of four, sits in a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: A Panda car was the British name for a small police patrol car, once painted in blue and white.
explanation.definitionFit: Panda cars were British police patrol vehicles, so a Panda is a type of police vehicle.

clue.text: An opening hotel missed housing odd associate

parts.note: an gives A

indicators.note: the outer letters house the word for odd, holding it inside
the letter for hotel is missed out of the word

parts.note: an opening is a chance or opportunity
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
quaint means odd or old-fashioned

explanation.surface: A hotel misses an opportunity while sheltering a strange guest.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing H from CHANCE leaves CANCE; A plus CANCE holds QUAINT.
explanation.definitionFit: An acquaintance is a person one knows slightly, an associate rather than a close friend.

clue.text: Foil lining trays too generously

indicators.note: the letters line the inside of these words, running across them

explanation.surface: Kitchen foil spread too lavishly over baking trays.
explanation.walkthrough: Foil seems to be kitchen foil; it is a comic's partner who sets up jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A stooge is a performer who serves as the butt or foil for a comedian.

clue.text: Distilled product of unknown make?

parts.note: a make, as of car, is a brand
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A mystery about which manufacturer made a distilled spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine or fermented fruit juice.

clue.text: Soldiers capturing American base

indicators.note: the soldiers capture the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Troops seize an American military base.
explanation.definitionFit: Base and mean are both adjectives for something low and contemptible in character.

clue.text: Police almost there crashed aircraft

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so these letters are rearranged
almost means the word falls one letter short, losing its end

explanation.surface: Police nearly arrived when an aircraft came down.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicopter is a rotary-winged aircraft, the type police often use for surveillance.

clue.text: Topless Victor becomes intimate

indicators.note: topless means the first letter, at the top of a down entry, is removed

parts.note: a victor is a winner

explanation.surface: A man called Victor going topless gets cosy with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Victor looks like a name (or the NATO V); it is a winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner and intimate both describe private, deeply personal feelings.

clue.text: Soldier dropping in standard initially achieved

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of achieved

explanation.surface: A soldier who drops in achieves the expected standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping in' sounds like visiting; it is parachuting.
explanation.definitionFit: A para is a paratrooper, a soldier who arrives by parachute.

clue.text: Second time heretic becomes bigoted

parts.note: an Arian followed the heresy of Arius, who denied Christ's full divinity

explanation.surface: Someone who lapses into heresy a second time turns intolerant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sectarian describes narrow prejudice rooted in membership of a religious faction.

clue.text: Goodness found in an oak seed

indicators.note: the exclamation is found inside the other word, set within it

parts.note: taken as written
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like goodness!

explanation.surface: Something good turns up inside an oak's seed.
explanation.walkthrough: Cor (as in 'cor blimey') is a British expression of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the nut of the oak tree, containing its seed.

clue.text: Small turtle leaving soft ground

indicators.note: the letter for soft leaves the word, so it is removed

parts.note: a terrapin is a small freshwater turtle
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: A little turtle crawls off soft earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of land considered for its physical features, ground in that sense.

clue.text: Bird colony in castle by eastern railway

parts.note: rook is another name for the castle in chess

explanation.surface: Birds nesting in a castle beside an eastern rail line.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookery is a breeding colony of rooks, a crow species that nests in groups.
